topics.h: Who makes you laugh at home? Who tells you stories? Your family is your first team!
p: A family is a group of people who live together, love and care for each other.
Some families are small, with parents and children. Some are big, with grandparents, uncles, aunts and cousins too.
A family where grandparents, uncles, aunts and cousins live together under one roof is called a joint family.
Family members share work at home, like cooking, cleaning, shopping and caring for the old and the young.
Every family is different, and every family is special.

ex.q: Think it through: Dadi has a bad knee and cannot climb stairs. How can the family help her?
st: Dadi needs things from the upper floor.
Children can fetch things for her.
Parents can take her to the doctor.
When everyone helps a little, Dadi feels cared for.
ex.a: Each member helps in a small way, so the whole family takes care of Dadi.

topics.rl: When you set the plates before dinner or water the plants, you are sharing family work.

topics.h: Who brings your letters? Who fixes a leaking tap? Lots of people help us every day!
p: A community is a group of families who live in the same area, like a village, a colony or a town.
People in a community help each other and celebrate festivals and fairs together.
Community helpers do work that everyone needs: farmers, doctors, nurses, teachers, postal workers and sanitation workers.
Electricians fix wires, plumbers fix pipes and taps, and carpenters make things from wood.
We should thank and respect every helper, because every job is important.

ex.q: Think it through: The water pipe in your colony bursts. Whom do the families call, and why?
st: Water is spilling and the taps are dry.
A plumber knows how to fix pipes.
The plumber mends the pipe.
Water comes back to every home.
ex.a: They call a plumber, because a plumber fixes water pipes and taps.

topics.rl: When neighbours share sweets at festivals or clean the park together, the community grows stronger.

topics.h: Your breakfast roti needed a farmer, a miller, a shopkeeper and a cook. Wow!
p: To depend means to need someone or something. Depending on each other is called interdependence.
People depend on each other: the farmer grows grain, the shopkeeper sells it and we buy it.
Animals depend on plants for food, shelter and air to breathe. Birds build nests in trees.
Plants also depend on animals: bees and butterflies carry pollen between flowers, and birds spread seeds.
Plants give out oxygen, which we breathe in. We breathe out carbon dioxide, which plants use to make food.

ex.q: Think it through: If all the bees in a mango orchard disappeared, what might happen to the mangoes?
st: Bees carry pollen from flower to flower.
Flowers need pollen to make fruits.
Without bees, fewer flowers get pollen.
So fewer mangoes grow.
ex.a: Fewer mangoes would grow, because plants depend on bees to carry pollen.

topics.rl: Next time you eat a banana, think of the farmer, the truck driver and the fruit seller who brought it to you.

topics.h: Take a walk around your street. How many useful places can you spot?
p: The area around our home is our neighbourhood.
A neighbourhood has many useful places: a school, a market, a hospital, a post office, a bank, a park and a police station.
Each place meets a need. We buy vegetables at the market and post letters at the post office.
Public places like parks, roads and libraries belong to everyone, so we must keep them clean.
In an emergency in India, we can call 112 for help.

ex.q: Think it through: Neha wants to borrow a storybook for free. Which place in her neighbourhood should she visit?
st: She wants to borrow, not buy.
A shop sells books, so she would have to pay.
A library lends books to read and return.
ex.a: The library.

topics.rl: Draw your own walk from home to school and mark every useful place you pass.

topics.h: The sun can be your guide! Where does it come up in the morning?
p: There are four main directions: North, East, South and West.
The sun rises in the East and sets in the West.
If you face North, East is on your right, West is on your left and South is behind you.
Between the main directions are North-East, South-East, South-West and North-West.
A compass has a needle that points North. Travellers and sailors use it to find their way.

ex.q: Think it through: Ravi faces the rising sun in the morning. Which direction is on his left?
st: The sun rises in the East, so Ravi faces East.
When you face East, North is on your left.
South is on your right and West is behind.
ex.a: North is on his left.

topics.rl: Stand in your courtyard in the morning, face the sun and point out all four directions.

topics.h: A map is like a bird's photo of your town, taken from high above!
p: A map is a drawing of a place as seen from above.
Maps use small pictures called symbols to show things like schools, roads, trees and rivers.
The key (or legend) of a map tells us what each symbol means.
On most maps, North is at the top, South at the bottom, East on the right and West on the left.
A map is much smaller than the real place, but it shows where things are.

ex.q: Think it through: On a map, the school is at the top and the park is at the bottom. Where is the park from the school?
st: On a map, the top is North and the bottom is South.
The park is below the school.
So the park is to the South of the school.
ex.a: The park is South of the school.

topics.rl: Ask an adult to show you a map on a phone or in an atlas. Find the arrow or letter N that shows North.

topics.h: Rub a leaf, sniff a flower, touch the bark. Plants are full of surprises!
p: Trees are tall plants with one thick, hard, woody stem called a trunk, like neem, mango and banyan.
Shrubs are medium-sized plants with many hard stems close to the ground, like rose and hibiscus (gudhal).
Herbs are small plants with soft green stems, like coriander (dhania), mint (pudina) and wheat.
Climbers have weak stems and climb up with support, like the money plant and the pea plant. Creepers spread on the ground, like pumpkin and watermelon.
We can observe leaves, bark, flowers and fruits by looking, touching gently and smelling, without plucking them.

ex.q: Think it through: A plant in Asha's garden is small, with a soft green stem. Its leaves smell fresh and are used in chutney. What kind of plant is it?
st: It is small with a soft green stem.
Small plants with soft green stems are herbs.
Mint and coriander are herbs used in chutney.
ex.a: It is a herb, like mint or coriander.

topics.rl: On a nature walk, place a paper on a leaf and rub it gently with a crayon. The leaf's veins will appear like magic!

topics.h: Shh! Sit still and listen. Can you hear a bird, a bee or a cricket?
p: Insects have 6 legs and 3 main body parts. Ants, bees and butterflies are insects.
Spiders have 8 legs, so they are not insects.
Birds have feathers and beaks. The shape of a beak suits the food a bird eats.
A butterfly grows in four stages: egg, caterpillar, pupa and adult butterfly.
We observe animals quietly from a distance. We never disturb nests, eggs or baby animals.

ex.q: Think it through: A kingfisher has a long, pointed beak. What food is it best for?
st: A long, pointed beak is like a spear.
It can grab slippery things quickly.
Kingfishers dive into water to catch fish.
ex.a: Catching fish from the water.

topics.rl: Keep a nature diary. Each morning, write down the birds you see or hear near your home.

topics.t: Biodiversity: so many kinds of life
topics.h: From tiny ants to giant elephants, India is home to an amazing variety of life!
p: Biodiversity means the great variety of plants and animals found in a place.
Different animals and plants live in different places: forests, deserts, rivers, seas and mountains.
Kaziranga National Park in Assam is famous for the one-horned rhinoceros. Gir in Gujarat is the home of Asiatic lions.
The Sundarbans in West Bengal have mangrove forests and the Royal Bengal tiger. Snow leopards live high in the Himalayas.
The tiger is India's national animal, the peacock is our national bird and the lotus is our national flower.

ex.q: Think it through: A forest has many kinds of trees, birds, insects and animals. Why is this good?
st: Each living thing has a job in nature.
Bees help flowers, birds spread seeds, and trees give shelter.
If many kinds live together, nature stays balanced and healthy.
ex.a: A forest with high biodiversity stays healthy because living things help each other.

topics.rl: Count how many different kinds of birds, insects and plants you can see in a park. That is the biodiversity of your park!

topics.h: Honey, bamboo, fruits and fresh air: a forest is like a giant free gift shop!
p: A forest is a large area thickly covered with trees, bushes and other plants. Many animals live there.
Forests give us wood, bamboo, fruits, honey, gum and medicinal plants.
Many communities live in and near forests. They collect forest things carefully and take only what they need.
Leaves of the sal tree are stitched into plates and bowls called pattal and dona.
Tree roots hold the soil in place, and forests help keep the air clean and cool.

ex.q: Think it through: A hillside loses all its trees. When heavy rain comes, what happens to the soil?
st: Tree roots hold the soil together like a net.
Without trees, nothing holds the soil.
Rain water washes the loose soil away.
ex.a: The soil gets washed away, because there are no roots to hold it.

topics.rl: Look around your home. Which things came from a forest? Maybe your wooden chair, a bamboo basket or a jar of honey!

topics.h: Would you hug a tree to protect it? Some brave people did just that!
p: The Bishnoi community of Rajasthan follows rules that say green trees must not be cut and animals must be protected.
In 1730, Amrita Devi Bishnoi of Khejarli village in Rajasthan hugged khejri trees to stop them from being cut. Many villagers joined her.
Bishnois also protect animals like the blackbuck and the chinkara.
In the 1970s, villagers in the hills of Uttarakhand, many of them women, hugged trees to stop them from being cut. This was called the Chipko movement.
'Chipko' means 'to stick' or 'to hug'. Gaura Devi led the women of Reni village in this movement in 1974.

ex.q: Think it through: Why did the villagers in the Chipko movement hug the trees?
st: Workers had come to cut down the trees.
The trees gave the villagers firewood and fodder, and held the soil on the slopes.
By hugging the trees, the villagers stood between the workers and the trees.
ex.a: To stop the trees from being cut, because the forest was important for their lives.

topics.rl: You can be a nature protector too: save paper, water your school plants and never harm birds or animals.

topics.h: One man planted a whole forest by himself! You can start with one seed.
p: Some communities keep patches of forest as sacred groves. No one cuts trees there, so plants and animals stay safe.
Sacred groves are found in many states, like the kavu of Kerala, the devrai of Maharashtra and the forest of Mawphlang in Meghalaya.
Jadav Payeng of Assam planted trees on a sandy island in the Brahmaputra for many years. It grew into a big forest called the Molai forest.
Saalumarada Thimmakka of Karnataka planted and cared for hundreds of banyan trees along a road.
Van Mahotsav is a tree-planting festival held in the first week of July. World Environment Day is on 5 June.

ex.q: Think it through: Why do people plant trees in the first week of July for Van Mahotsav?
st: In July, the monsoon rains have begun in most of India.
Young plants need lots of water to grow roots.
Rain waters the saplings naturally.
ex.a: Because the rainy season gives young saplings plenty of water to grow.

topics.rl: Plant a sapling with your family, give it a name and water it every week. Watch it grow along with you!

topics.h: Your body is like a busy factory. Food brings in the workers that keep it running!
p: Nutrients are the useful parts of food that help our body work, grow and stay healthy.
Carbohydrates give us energy. Rice, wheat, potatoes and bajra are rich in carbohydrates.
Proteins help our body grow and repair itself. Dal, rajma, milk, paneer, eggs and fish are rich in proteins.
Fats also give energy. Ghee, butter, oil and nuts have fats. We need them only in small amounts.
Vitamins and minerals protect us from illness. Fruits and vegetables are full of them. Milk gives calcium for strong bones and teeth.

ex.q: Think it through: Raju plays football for two hours and feels tired. Which food will give him energy quickly: a banana or a glass of water?
st: Energy comes from carbohydrates.
A banana has carbohydrates.
Water is very important, but it gives no energy.
ex.a: The banana, because it has carbohydrates that give energy.

topics.rl: Look at your lunch box. Can you find one energy food, one body-building food and one protective food?

topics.h: A good plate is like a good team: everyone plays a part!
p: A balanced diet has all the nutrients in the right amounts: carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins and minerals.
We also need roughage (fibre) and water. Roughage from fruits, vegetables and whole grains helps us digest food.
A thali with roti or rice, dal, a green vegetable, curd and salad is a balanced meal.
Too much fried food, sweets, chips and fizzy drinks is not good for health.
Wash hands before eating, eat slowly, chew well and do not waste food.

ex.q: Think it through: Tanya's lunch is a plate of rice and potato curry. What should she add to make it more balanced?
st: Rice and potato both give mostly carbohydrates.
She needs proteins, so she can add dal or curd.
She needs vitamins, minerals and roughage, so she can add a green vegetable or salad.
ex.a: Add dal or curd and a green vegetable or salad.

topics.rl: Help plan one day's meals at home. Try to fit all the food groups in!

topics.h: Idli in Chennai, dhokla in Ahmedabad, litti chokha in Patna: India is a giant tasty menu!
p: Food in each region depends on the crops that grow there and the weather.
Rice grows well where there is a lot of rain, so it is a main food in many coastal and eastern states like Kerala, West Bengal, Odisha and Assam.
Wheat is a main food in Punjab and Haryana. Bajra grows in dry Rajasthan, and ragi is popular in Karnataka.
People living near the sea or rivers often eat fish, like machher jhol in West Bengal and fish curry in Goa and Kerala.
Millets like bajra, jowar and ragi need less water and are very healthy. The year 2023 was the International Year of Millets.

ex.q: Think it through: Why is coconut used so much in Kerala food?
st: Kerala is on the coast and gets heavy rain.
Coconut trees grow very well in warm, wet coastal places.
People cook with what grows near them.
ex.a: Because coconut trees grow well in Kerala's warm, rainy coastal weather.

topics.rl: Ask your grandparents what they ate as children. Is it the same as the food of your region today?

topics.h: Germs are too tiny to see, but soap and water can chase them away!
p: Germs are tiny living things that can make us ill. We cannot see them with our eyes.
Wash your hands with soap and water for at least 20 seconds, before eating and after using the toilet.
Brush your teeth twice a day, bathe every day, keep nails short and wear clean clothes.
Cover your mouth and nose with a tissue or your elbow when you cough or sneeze.
Drink clean, safe water. Do not let water collect in old tyres or pots, because mosquitoes breed in still water.

ex.q: Think it through: Ishaan played in the mud and now wants to eat a samosa. What should he do first, and why?
st: His hands touched mud, which may have germs.
If he eats now, the germs can go into his mouth.
Washing with soap removes the germs.
ex.a: He should wash his hands with soap and water, so germs do not enter his body with the food.

topics.rl: Hum 'Happy Birthday' twice while washing your hands. That takes about 20 seconds!

topics.h: Kho-kho, kabaddi, cycling or skipping: your body loves to move!
p: Exercise and outdoor play make our muscles, heart and bones strong.
Children should be active for about one hour (60 minutes) every day.
Yoga helps the body bend and stretch and calms the mind. International Day of Yoga is on 21 June.
Sleep helps the body rest and grow. Children your age need about 9 to 12 hours of sleep every night.
Too much screen time and sitting still for long is not good. Take breaks to move and play.

ex.q: Think it through: Neel plays outside for 25 minutes and does yoga for 15 minutes. How many more minutes should he be active to reach 60 minutes?
st: 25 + 15 = 40 minutes so far.
60 − 40 = 20 minutes more.
ex.a: 20 more minutes.

topics.rl: Make a weekly play chart at home. Tick each day you play outside for an hour.

topics.h: Happy, sad, angry, scared, excited: feelings are like the weather inside us!
p: Everyone has feelings, like happy, sad, angry, scared, worried and excited. All feelings are normal.
Talking about our feelings to a trusted adult, like a parent, grandparent or teacher, helps us feel better.
When angry, we can take slow deep breaths, count to ten or walk away for a while before we speak.
Being kind, sharing and including others makes everyone feel happy and safe.
If someone bullies you or touches you in a way that feels unsafe, say 'No', move away and tell a trusted adult.

ex.q: Think it through: Zoya is upset because her drawing got torn. What can she do to feel better?
st: It is normal to feel sad or upset.
She can take a few deep breaths to calm down.
She can talk to her mother or teacher about it.
She might fix the drawing with tape or make a new one.
ex.a: Calm down with deep breaths, talk to a trusted adult, and then try to fix or redo the drawing.

topics.rl: Make a feelings chart. Each evening, draw a face that shows how you felt that day.

topics.h: How can a small child lift a big friend on a seesaw? The secret is a simple machine!
p: A simple machine is a tool that makes work easier. It helps us lift, move or cut things with less effort.
A lever is a strong bar that turns on a fixed point called the fulcrum. A seesaw, a hand pump handle and a bottle opener are levers.
A pair of scissors is made of two levers joined at a point.
A wheel and axle is a wheel fixed to a rod. Bicycle wheels and bullock cart wheels help us move loads easily.
A pulley is a wheel with a groove for a rope. Pulling the rope down lifts a load up, like a bucket from a well or a flag up a pole.

ex.q: Think it through: Why is it easier to raise the flag on Independence Day using a pulley at the top of the pole?
st: The flag must go up a tall pole.
Climbing the pole would be hard and unsafe.
With a pulley, we pull the rope down from the ground.
The pulley turns that pull into an upward lift.
ex.a: The pulley lets us pull down from the ground to send the flag up, which is easier and safer.

topics.rl: Look at a hand pump. Pushing the long handle down lifts water up. The handle is a lever!

topics.h: Why do workers roll heavy drums up a plank instead of lifting them? Let us find out!
p: A ramp, or inclined plane, is a sloping surface. It makes it easier to move heavy things up or down.
A slide in the park and a sloping path into a building are ramps.
A wedge is thick at one end and thin or sharp at the other. It is used to cut or split things, like a knife or an axe.
A screw is a rod with a groove that winds around it. The lid of a jar works like a screw.
Using a ramp, we push with less effort, but we move the load over a longer distance.

ex.q: Think it through: Why do many schools and hospitals have a ramp beside the stairs?
st: Some people use wheelchairs, prams or trolleys.
Wheels cannot easily go up steps.
A ramp is a smooth slope that wheels can roll up.
So everyone can enter the building.
ex.a: A ramp lets people in wheelchairs and with trolleys move up easily, so everyone can enter.

topics.rl: Watch a fruit seller cut a watermelon. The knife is a wedge that splits the fruit!

topics.h: Kick a ball, open a door, fly a kite: every move starts with a push or a pull!
p: A push or a pull is called a force. Forces make things move, stop or change direction.
We push a shopping trolley to move it and pull a drawer to open it.
A force can also change the shape of things, like pressing clay or squeezing a sponge.
Things move in different ways: in a straight line (a train on a straight track), round and round (a merry-go-round) and to and fro (a swing).
Rolling is easier than sliding. That is why wheels help. A ball rolls farther on a smooth floor than on rough grass.

ex.q: Think it through: Sana pushes a toy car on a smooth tiled floor and then on a rough carpet with the same push. Where will it go farther?
st: A rough surface rubs more against the wheels.
This rubbing slows the car down.
A smooth floor rubs less.
ex.a: On the smooth tiled floor, because rough surfaces slow things down more.

topics.rl: At the park, notice the swing going to and fro, the merry-go-round going round and round and the slide sending you down in a straight line.

topics.h: Your cotton shirt was once a fluffy white ball growing on a plant!
p: A raw material is the basic thing from which something new is made.
The new thing made from it is called a product. Cotton is a raw material, and a shirt is a product.
Many raw materials come from plants: cotton, wood, bamboo, sugarcane and jute.
Some come from animals, like milk, wool and silk. Others come from the earth, like clay, sand and iron.
Glass is made from sand, paper from wood or bamboo pulp, and jaggery (gur) from sugarcane juice.

ex.q: Think it through: Which raw material is used to make a clay diya for Diwali, and where does it come from?
st: A diya is made of baked clay.
Clay is a kind of soft, sticky soil.
So it comes from the earth.
ex.a: Clay, which comes from the earth.

topics.rl: Pick any five things in your kitchen. Can you guess the raw material each one was made from?

topics.h: A potter's wheel spins, wet clay rises, and a pot is born! Every product goes through steps.
p: Most products are made in steps, one after another.
Cotton to cloth: cotton is picked, the seeds are removed, the cotton is spun into thread, and the thread is woven into cloth on a loom.
Clay to pot: clay is mixed with water and kneaded, shaped on a potter's wheel, dried in the sun and then baked in a hot kiln to make it strong.
Wheat to roti: wheat is harvested, the grains are separated, ground into atta, kneaded into dough, rolled and cooked.
If the steps are done in the wrong order, the product will not come out right.

ex.q: Think it through: Why does a potter bake a pot after drying it?
st: Dried clay can still crack or soften in water.
Baking in a very hot kiln makes clay hard.
A hard, baked pot can hold water.
ex.a: Baking makes the pot hard and strong, so it can hold water without breaking.

topics.rl: Watch someone at home make rotis. Count the steps from atta to a hot, puffed roti!

topics.h: Painted elephants, wooden toys and bright tie-dye sarees: India is full of skilled hands!
p: A craft is something beautiful and useful made by skilled hands, often passed down in families.
Madhubani painting is from Bihar, Warli painting from Maharashtra and Pattachitra from Odisha.
Channapatna in Karnataka is famous for colourful wooden toys. Jaipur in Rajasthan is famous for blue pottery.
Kanchipuram in Tamil Nadu is known for silk sarees. Bandhani, a tie-and-dye cloth, comes from Gujarat and Rajasthan.
Handloom and cottage industries make things by hand at home or in small workshops. Factories use big machines to make many things quickly.

ex.q: Think it through: A factory makes 1,000 plain cups in an hour. An artist paints 10 cups by hand in a day. Why might people still buy the hand-painted cups?
st: Factory cups are all the same and quick to make.
Each hand-painted cup is special and shows the artist's skill.
Buying crafts also helps artists earn and keeps old skills alive.
ex.a: Because each handmade piece is special, and buying it supports artists and keeps the craft alive.

topics.rl: Look at a fair or a local market. Can you spot a handmade craft from your own state?

topics.h: Hot sand, very little rain and camels walking slowly: welcome to the Thar Desert!
p: A desert is a dry place that gets very little rain. The Thar Desert is mostly in Rajasthan.
In a hot desert, days are very hot, but nights can be cold.
Many desert houses have thick mud walls and small windows, which keep the inside cool by day. In Kutch, Gujarat, round mud houses are called bhungas.
People save every drop of water. They collect rainwater in underground tanks and step-wells.
The camel is called the ship of the desert. Its wide, padded feet do not sink in sand, and its hump stores fat, not water.

ex.q: Think it through: Why do people in the desert wear loose cotton clothes and turbans?
st: The desert sun is very hot.
Loose cotton clothes let air flow and keep the body cool.
A turban or a covering protects the head from the hot sun and dusty winds.
ex.a: To stay cool and protect themselves from the hot sun and dust.

topics.rl: If you visit Jaisalmer or Bikaner, look for thick-walled houses, camels and water tanks.

topics.t: Life in the hills and mountains
topics.h: Snowy peaks, step-like fields and yaks with long hair: let us climb the Himalayas!
p: Hills and mountains are high lands. Places high up are cooler, and some get snow in winter.
Many houses in the hills have sloping roofs, so rain and snow slide off easily. They are often made of wood and stone.
On slopes, farmers cut flat steps into the hillside for farming. This is called terrace farming.
Apples grow in Himachal Pradesh and Jammu and Kashmir. Tea grows on the hills of Darjeeling and the Nilgiris.
People wear warm woollen clothes. In the high Himalayas, yaks give milk, wool and carry loads.

ex.q: Think it through: Why do farmers in the hills make step-like fields?
st: On a steep slope, rain water rushes down.
Rushing water washes away soil and seeds.
Flat steps slow the water and hold the soil.
ex.a: Flat steps stop the soil and water from rushing down the slope, so crops can grow.

topics.rl: Look at pictures of Shimla, Gangtok or Munnar. Spot the sloping roofs and green step fields!

topics.h: Waves splash, boats sail out and coconut trees sway: let us visit the seaside!
p: The coast is land next to the sea. India has a long coastline on the west, the east and the south.
Coastal places are often warm and humid (damp air). Many get heavy rain in the monsoon.
Many people living on the coast catch fish, build boats, and grow coconut and rice.
Salt is made from sea water. The sea water is left in shallow pans, the sun dries it, and salt is left behind. Gujarat makes the most salt in India.
Kerala's backwaters are famous for houseboats. Many coastal houses have sloping roofs for the heavy rain.

ex.q: Think it through: How does the sun help make salt from sea water?
st: Sea water is let into shallow, flat pans.
The sun heats the water and it slowly dries up (evaporates).
The salt cannot dry up, so it is left behind as white crystals.
ex.a: The sun dries up the water, and the salt is left behind.

topics.rl: Next time you add salt to your dal, remember it may have come from the sea and the sun!

topics.h: Why does a camel have long eyelashes, and why do some houses in Assam stand on stilts?
p: Climate is the usual weather of a place over many years: hot or cold, wet or dry.
To adapt means to change our ways to suit the place we live in. People adapt their houses, clothes, food and work.
In parts of Assam that flood often, some houses are built on bamboo stilts so water can flow under them.
Animals adapt too: camels have long eyelashes to keep out sand, and yaks have thick long hair to stay warm.
Ladakh is a cold desert. It is very cold and dry, with little rain. Pashmina goats there grow very soft, warm wool.

ex.q: Think it through: Why would a stilt house be useful in a place that floods?
st: During floods, water rises over the ground.
A house on the ground would fill with water.
A house on tall stilts stays above the water.
ex.a: The house stays above the flood water, so the family and their things stay dry.

topics.rl: Compare your clothes in summer and winter. You adapt to the weather too!

topics.t: The sun, the moon and the stars
topics.h: Look up! By day the sun shines, and at night the moon and thousands of stars twinkle.
p: The sun is a star. It is the star nearest to the Earth, and it gives us light and heat.
The sun looks small only because it is very far away. It is much, much bigger than the Earth.
The moon goes around the Earth. It has no light of its own. It shines because sunlight falls on it and bounces back to us.

Stars are huge, hot balls of glowing gas. They look tiny because they are very, very far away. Groups of stars that make patterns are called constellations. The Saptarishi is a famous pattern of seven bright stars.
Never look straight at the sun, not even with sunglasses. It can badly hurt your eyes.

ex.q: Think it through: Stars are in the sky during the day too. Why can't we see them?
st: The stars are still there in the daytime.
The sun is so close and bright that its light fills the sky.
The faint starlight is hidden by the bright sunlight.
ex.a: The bright sunlight hides the much fainter light of the stars.

topics.rl: On a clear night, away from city lights, look for the seven bright stars of the Saptarishi. With an adult, see if you can spot the Pole Star.

topics.h: The sun seems to rise and set, but it is actually the Earth that is spinning!
p: The Earth is shaped like a ball (a sphere). It spins around itself all the time, like a top.
The side of the Earth facing the sun has day. The side facing away from the sun has night.
One full spin takes about 24 hours. That gives us one day and one night.
Because the Earth spins from west to east, the sun seems to rise in the east and set in the west.
The Earth also goes around the sun. One full trip takes about 365 days, which is one year.

ex.q: Think it through: Your cousin lives in America. When you are going to school in the morning in India, she is getting ready for bed. Why?
st: The Earth is a ball that spins.
Only half of it faces the sun at a time.
India and America are on different sides of the Earth.
When India faces the sun, much of America faces away from it.
ex.a: Because when India has day, America is on the side of the Earth facing away from the sun, so it has night.

topics.rl: In a dark room, with an adult, shine a torch on a ball and turn it slowly. Watch day and night move around the ball!

topics.h: Some nights the moon is a thin smile, some nights a full round plate. Is it really changing shape?
p: The moon does not really change its shape. Half of it is always lit by the sun.
As the moon goes around the Earth, we see different amounts of its lit part. These changing shapes are called phases of the moon.
On the new moon night (Amavasya), we cannot see the moon. On the full moon night (Purnima), we see a full round moon.
After the new moon, the lit part grows night by night: crescent, half moon, then full moon. After the full moon, it shrinks again.
From one full moon to the next takes about 29 and a half days, nearly a month.

ex.q: Think it through: Tonight is a full moon. About how many days until the next full moon?
st: The moon takes about 29 and a half days to go through all its phases.
So the next full moon comes after about 29 or 30 days.
ex.a: About 29 to 30 days, nearly a month.

topics.rl: Keep a moon diary for a month. Each night, draw the moon's shape and watch it grow and shrink.

qa.q: Aman lives with his parents, his grandparents, his uncle, aunt and two cousins. What kind of family is this?
qa.e: Many relatives like grandparents, uncles and aunts living together make a joint family.

qa.q: Which of these is a good way for a child to help at home?
qa.e: Folding dry clothes is a small job that helps the whole family.

qa.q: What makes a group of people a family?
qa.a: They live together and care for each other
qa.e: A family is about living together, love and care, not about looks or likes.

qa.q: Meera lives with her mother, her father and her baby brother. How many people are in her family, counting Meera?
qa.e: Mother, father, baby brother and Meera make 4 people.

qa.q: Nanaji cannot read small letters well. How can Riya help him?
qa.a: Read the newspaper aloud to him
qa.e: Reading aloud is a kind way to help an older family member.

qa.q: Why do family members share housework?
qa.a: So that work gets done and no one is too tired
qa.e: When work is shared, it gets done quickly and everyone gets time to rest and play.

qa.q: Which of these is true about families?
qa.a: Families can be different, but each one is special
qa.e: Families come in many sizes and kinds. Each family is special in its own way.

qa.q: Kabir's mother is unwell. Which is the kindest thing Kabir can do?
qa.a: Bring her a glass of water and let her rest
qa.e: Bringing water and letting her rest shows care for a sick family member.

qa.q: What is a community?
qa.a: A group of families living in the same area
qa.e: A community is made of many families living in one place, like a village or colony.

qa.q: The fan in your classroom stops working because of a loose wire. Who should fix it?
qa.e: An electrician knows how to fix wires, switches and fans safely.

qa.q: Who keeps our streets clean by collecting garbage?
qa.e: Sanitation workers collect garbage and keep our area clean and healthy.

qa.q: In Riya's village, everyone gathers to celebrate the harvest festival. This shows that people in a community…
qa.a: come together and share happy times
qa.e: Celebrating together brings people of a community closer.

qa.q: Which helper grows the rice and wheat that we eat?
qa.e: Farmers grow food crops like rice, wheat and vegetables.

qa.q: Why should we respect every community helper?
qa.a: Because every job is important for the community
qa.e: We need all kinds of work, so every helper and every job deserves respect.

qa.q: Pooja's slipper strap breaks. Who can mend it?
qa.e: A cobbler mends shoes, slippers and bags.

qa.q: Which is a good way to help your community?
qa.a: Helping clean the park with neighbours
qa.e: Cleaning the park together keeps a shared place nice for everyone.

qa.q: What does interdependence mean?
qa.e: Interdependence means people, plants and animals need each other.

qa.q: How do bees help plants?
qa.a: They carry pollen from flower to flower
qa.e: When bees visit flowers for nectar, pollen sticks to them and goes to other flowers. This helps fruits form.

qa.q: Which gas do plants give out that we breathe in?
qa.e: Green plants give out oxygen. We need oxygen to breathe.

qa.q: A koel eats a ripe fruit and later drops the seed far away. A new plant grows there. How did the bird help?
qa.e: Birds that eat fruits drop seeds in new places, so new plants grow.

qa.q: Which of these shows people depending on each other?
qa.a: A tailor stitching a shirt for a farmer, who grows food for the tailor
qa.e: The tailor and the farmer each do work the other needs. That is interdependence.

qa.q: In the chain grass → deer → tiger, what does the deer depend on for food?
qa.e: The arrow shows who is eaten by whom. The deer eats grass.

qa.q: How does a farmer use cow dung?
qa.e: Cow dung is a natural manure. It makes the soil rich so crops grow well.

qa.q: If there were no trees near a village, which of these would be hardest for birds?
qa.e: Many birds build nests in trees. Without trees they lose their homes.

qa.q: Where would you go to send a rakhi to your cousin in another city?
qa.e: The post office sends letters and parcels to other places.

qa.q: Arjun has a high fever. Which place should his family take him to?
qa.e: Doctors and nurses at a hospital or clinic treat sick people.

qa.q: What is a neighbourhood?
qa.e: The streets, shops and places near our home make up our neighbourhood.

qa.q: Which number can you call for help in an emergency anywhere in India?
qa.e: 112 is India's single emergency number for police, fire and ambulance help.

qa.q: Which of these is a public place?
qa.e: A public park is shared by everyone in the community.

qa.q: Where do people keep their savings safe?
qa.e: A bank keeps our money safe and helps us save.

qa.q: A house is on fire! Which helpers rush to put it out?
qa.e: Firefighters from the fire station come with water and put out fires.

qa.q: Why should we keep public places clean?
qa.a: Because they belong to everyone and we all use them
qa.e: Public places are shared, so keeping them clean is everyone's job.

qa.q: How many main directions are there?
qa.e: The four main directions are North, East, South and West.

qa.q: In which direction does the sun set?
qa.e: The sun rises in the East and sets in the West.

qa.q: Sita faces North. What is on her right?
qa.e: When you face North, East is on your right hand side.

qa.q: Which direction is opposite to East?
qa.e: East and West are opposite each other.

qa.q: Which tool has a needle that always points North?
qa.e: A compass needle turns and settles pointing North, so we can find all directions.

qa.q: Arjun faces West. What is behind him?
qa.e: The direction behind you is opposite to the one you face. Opposite of West is East.

qa.q: What is the direction between South and West called?
qa.e: The direction between South and West is South-West.

qa.q: Meena faces South. Which direction is on her left?
qa.e: Facing South, your left hand points East and your right hand points West.

qa.q: What is a map?
qa.a: A drawing of a place as seen from above
qa.e: A map shows a place from above, as a bird would see it.

qa.q: What does the key of a map tell us?
qa.e: The map key, or legend, explains the symbols used on the map.

qa.q: On most maps, which direction is at the top?
qa.e: Most maps are drawn with North at the top.

qa.q: On a map with North at the top, the temple is on the right of the pond. In which direction is the temple from the pond?
qa.e: On a map with North at the top, the right side is East.

qa.q: Why do maps use symbols?
qa.a: To show many things clearly in a small space
qa.e: Symbols are small, simple pictures, so many things fit clearly on one map.

qa.q: On a map with North at the top, the market is at the bottom and the bus stand is at the top. Where is the market from the bus stand?
qa.e: The bottom of a map is South, so the market is South of the bus stand.

qa.q: A blue wavy line on a map most likely shows…
qa.e: Maps usually show rivers with blue wavy lines, like flowing water.

qa.q: How is a map different from the real place?
qa.e: A map is a small drawing, so a whole town can fit on one page.

qa.q: Which of these is a tree?
qa.e: A mango plant grows tall with a thick woody trunk, so it is a tree.

qa.q: A money plant grows up a wall with the help of a stick. What kind of plant is it?
qa.e: A money plant has a weak stem and climbs up with support, so it is a climber.

qa.q: Which part of a tree is the thick, hard stem?
qa.e: The thick, hard stem of a tree is called the trunk.

qa.q: A plant is medium-sized and has many hard stems near the ground. It grows red flowers. What is it?
qa.e: Medium plants with many hard stems close to the ground are shrubs, like the hibiscus.

qa.q: Which plant spreads along the ground because its stem is weak?
qa.e: A watermelon plant is a creeper. Its weak stem spreads along the ground.

qa.q: The banyan tree has roots that hang down from its branches into the soil. What do these roots do?
qa.a: They help hold up the big branches
qa.e: These hanging roots grow into the soil and act like pillars that support the wide branches.

qa.q: What is the best way to observe a flower on a nature trail?
qa.a: Look closely, smell it gently and leave it on the plant
qa.e: We can learn a lot just by looking and smelling. Leaving the flower lets bees visit it too.

qa.q: Which of these is a herb?
qa.e: Coriander is a small plant with a soft green stem, so it is a herb.

qa.q: How many legs does an insect have?
qa.e: All insects, like ants, bees and butterflies, have 6 legs.

qa.q: Why is a spider not an insect?
qa.e: Insects have 6 legs. Spiders have 8 legs, so they are not insects.

qa.q: A spider has 8 legs and an ant has 6 legs. How many more legs does the spider have?
qa.e: 8 − 6 = 2. A spider has 2 more legs than an ant.

qa.q: What comes out of a butterfly's egg?
qa.e: A caterpillar hatches from the egg. Later it becomes a pupa and then a butterfly.

qa.q: Which body covering do all birds have?
qa.e: Feathers are found only on birds. They keep birds warm and help most of them fly.

qa.q: A sunbird has a long, thin beak. What does it mostly feed on?
qa.e: A long, thin beak can reach deep inside flowers to sip sweet nectar.

qa.q: You spot a bird's nest with eggs in a bush. What should you do?
qa.e: Watching from far away keeps the eggs and the parent birds safe.

qa.q: Which stage of a butterfly's life comes just before the adult butterfly?
qa.e: The order is egg, caterpillar, pupa, butterfly. The pupa comes just before the butterfly.

qa.q: What does biodiversity mean?
qa.a: The variety of plants and animals in a place
qa.e: Bio means life and diversity means variety. Biodiversity is the variety of living things.

qa.q: Which national park in Assam is famous for the one-horned rhinoceros?
qa.e: Kaziranga in Assam is home to most of the world's one-horned rhinoceroses.

qa.q: Where in India do Asiatic lions live in the wild?
qa.e: Gir and the forests around it in Gujarat are the only wild home of Asiatic lions.

qa.q: Which is the national bird of India?
qa.e: The peacock (Indian peafowl) is India's national bird.

qa.q: The Sundarbans have special trees that grow in salty, muddy water near the sea. What are these forests called?
qa.e: Mangroves grow where rivers meet the sea. The Sundarbans have one of the largest mangrove forests.

qa.q: Which animal lives high in the cold, snowy Himalayas?
qa.e: The snow leopard has thick fur and lives in the cold Himalayan mountains.

qa.q: Which is the national flower of India?
qa.e: The lotus is India's national flower.

qa.q: Why is it important to protect the many kinds of plants and animals?
qa.a: Because living things depend on each other to keep nature balanced
qa.e: When one kind of living thing disappears, others that depend on it are harmed too.

qa.q: Which of these do we get from forests?
qa.e: Bees make honey in forests, and honey collectors gather it.

qa.q: How do tree roots help the soil?
qa.a: They hold the soil in place
qa.e: Roots spread through the soil like a net and stop rain from washing it away.

qa.q: Plates made by stitching sal leaves together are called…
qa.e: Pattal are plates made from leaves like sal. They are used at many meals and feasts.

qa.q: What happens to animals when a forest is cut down?
qa.a: They lose their homes and food
qa.e: Forests give animals food and shelter. Without trees, they have nowhere to live.

qa.q: Why do forest communities take only what they need from the forest?
qa.a: So that the forest can keep growing and giving
qa.e: If we take only a little, plants and trees can grow back, and the forest lasts for a long time.

qa.q: Which of these is NOT a forest product?
qa.e: Steel is made from iron in factories. Bamboo, gum and herbs come from forests.

qa.q: Which of these is a way forests help us?
qa.a: They give clean air and shade
qa.e: Trees give out oxygen and give shade. Forests keep the air cleaner and cooler.

qa.q: Bamboo from forests can be used to make…
qa.e: Bamboo is strong and bendy, so it is woven into baskets, mats and even houses.

qa.q: What did people do in the Chipko movement?
qa.a: They hugged trees to stop them from being cut
qa.e: In the Chipko movement, villagers held on to trees so that the trees could not be cut.

qa.q: The Chipko movement took place in the hills of which present-day state?
qa.e: The Chipko movement happened in the hills that are now in Uttarakhand.

qa.q: Amrita Devi Bishnoi protected khejri trees in which year?
qa.e: In 1730, Amrita Devi and the villagers of Khejarli hugged khejri trees to protect them.

qa.q: Which animals are the Bishnoi people famous for protecting?
qa.e: Bishnois care for the blackbuck and the chinkara, which roam near their villages in Rajasthan.

qa.q: What does the word 'Chipko' mean?
qa.e: Chipko means to stick or hug. People hugged the trees.

qa.q: Gaura Devi is remembered for…
qa.a: leading the women of Reni village to protect trees
qa.e: In 1974, Gaura Devi led the women of Reni village in the Chipko movement.

qa.q: The Bishnoi community follows a rule about trees. What is it?
qa.e: One of the Bishnoi rules is not to cut green, living trees.

qa.q: Why were the trees important to the villagers of the Chipko movement?
qa.a: They gave firewood, fodder and held the soil
qa.e: The forest gave the villagers firewood and fodder for their animals, and kept the soil safe.

qa.q: What is a sacred grove?
qa.a: A patch of forest that a community protects
qa.e: Sacred groves are forest patches that communities protect. Trees there are not cut.

qa.q: Who grew the Molai forest in Assam?
qa.e: Jadav Payeng planted trees on a sandy island of the Brahmaputra for years, and the Molai forest grew.

qa.q: When is World Environment Day celebrated?
qa.e: World Environment Day is celebrated every year on 5 June.

qa.q: Van Mahotsav is a festival of…
qa.e: During Van Mahotsav, people plant saplings all over India.

qa.q: Saalumarada Thimmakka is famous for…
qa.a: planting and caring for banyan trees along a road
qa.e: Saalumarada Thimmakka of Karnataka planted hundreds of banyan trees and cared for them like children.

qa.q: In which month is Van Mahotsav held?
qa.e: Van Mahotsav is held in the first week of July, during the rains.

qa.q: Why are plants and animals safe in a sacred grove?
qa.a: Because people do not cut trees or harm living things there
qa.e: The community protects the grove, so trees and the animals living there are left in peace.

qa.q: Which is the best way for a child to care for nature?
qa.a: Planting a sapling and watering it
qa.e: Planting and caring for a sapling helps nature grow.

qa.q: Which nutrient mainly gives us energy?
qa.e: Carbohydrates in foods like rice, roti and potatoes give us energy to work and play.

qa.q: Which food is rich in protein?
qa.e: Dals like moong are rich in proteins, which help the body grow.

qa.q: Why do we need vitamins and minerals?
qa.e: Vitamins and minerals keep our body working well and help protect us from falling ill.

qa.q: Which of these is rich in fat?
qa.e: Ghee is almost all fat. We need fats only in small amounts.

qa.q: Milk is good for strong bones and teeth because it has…
qa.e: Milk, curd and paneer have calcium, a mineral that builds strong bones and teeth.

qa.q: Amla and oranges are rich in which vitamin?
qa.e: Amla, oranges and lemons are rich in vitamin C, which helps fight illness.

qa.q: Our body can make vitamin D when our skin gets…
qa.e: When sunlight falls on our skin, the body makes vitamin D. It also helps bones stay strong.

qa.q: Which group of foods helps our body grow?
qa.e: Eggs, fish, paneer and dal are rich in proteins, the body-building nutrient.

qa.q: What is a balanced diet?
qa.a: Food with all the nutrients in the right amounts
qa.e: A balanced diet gives the body all the nutrients it needs in the right amounts.

qa.q: Which meal is the most balanced?
qa.a: Roti, dal, green vegetable, curd and salad
qa.e: This thali has carbohydrates, proteins, vitamins, minerals and roughage.

qa.q: What does roughage do for us?
qa.e: Roughage, or fibre, helps food move through the body and keeps the stomach healthy.

qa.q: Which of these is rich in roughage?
qa.e: Fruits like guava, especially with their skin, are rich in fibre.

qa.q: Why should we not eat too much fried food and sweets?
qa.a: They are bad for health if eaten too much
qa.e: Too much oil and sugar can harm our teeth, heart and weight.

qa.q: Arun's dinner is roti and dal. Which item adds vitamins and roughage?
qa.e: Vegetables add vitamins, minerals and roughage to the meal.

qa.q: Which is a good eating habit?
qa.a: Chewing food well and eating slowly
qa.e: Chewing well helps digestion, and eating slowly helps us enjoy food.

qa.q: Besides food, what else must we drink plenty of every day?
qa.e: Clean water keeps our body working well, especially on hot days.

qa.q: Dhokla is a well-known dish from which state?
qa.e: Dhokla is a soft, steamed snack from Gujarat.

qa.q: Why is rice a main food in states like Kerala and West Bengal?
qa.a: Because rice grows well where there is a lot of rain
qa.e: Rice fields need a lot of water, and these states get heavy rain.

qa.q: Bajra is grown in Rajasthan because…
qa.e: Bajra is a millet that grows well in hot, dry places with little rain.

qa.q: Which dish is from Bihar?
qa.e: Litti chokha, baked wheat balls with mashed vegetables, is a famous dish of Bihar.

qa.q: The International Year of Millets was celebrated in which year?
qa.e: The United Nations named 2023 the International Year of Millets. India suggested the idea.

qa.q: People living near the sea in Goa often eat…
qa.e: Fish is easy to get near the sea, so fish curry with rice is popular in Goa.

qa.q: Which of these is a millet?
qa.e: Ragi, bajra and jowar are millets. Rice and wheat are other grains.

qa.q: Makki di roti and sarson da saag are a famous winter meal of…
qa.e: This meal of maize roti and mustard greens is loved in Punjab.

qa.q: For how many seconds should we rub our hands with soap?
qa.e: Rubbing hands with soap for at least 20 seconds removes most germs.

qa.q: How many times a day should we brush our teeth?
qa.e: Brushing in the morning and at night keeps teeth and gums healthy.

qa.q: What is the best way to cover a sneeze?
qa.a: Sneeze into your elbow or a tissue
qa.e: Using your elbow or a tissue stops germs from spreading to others and to things you touch.

qa.q: Mosquitoes lay their eggs in…
qa.a: still water in pots and tyres
qa.e: Mosquitoes breed in still water. Emptying pots and tyres helps stop them.

qa.q: When must you wash your hands?
qa.a: Before eating and after using the toilet
qa.e: Germs can be on hands even when they look clean, so we wash before eating and after the toilet.

qa.q: Why should we keep our nails short and clean?
qa.a: Dirt and germs can hide under long nails
qa.e: Germs collect under long nails and can go into our mouth while eating.

qa.q: Why can't we see germs?
qa.a: They are too tiny for our eyes
qa.e: Germs are so tiny that we need a microscope to see them.

qa.q: Which water is safe to drink?
qa.e: Boiling or filtering water kills or removes germs, making it safe to drink.

qa.q: About how long should children be active every day?
qa.e: Children should play or exercise actively for about 60 minutes, or one hour, every day.

qa.q: On which date is International Day of Yoga celebrated?
qa.e: International Day of Yoga is celebrated every year on 21 June.

qa.q: Why do we need sleep?
qa.a: To help the body rest and grow
qa.e: During sleep the body rests, repairs itself and grows.

qa.q: Diya sleeps from 9 pm to 7 am. How many hours does she sleep?
qa.e: From 9 pm to 12 midnight is 3 hours, and from 12 to 7 am is 7 hours. 3 + 7 = 10 hours.

qa.q: Which of these is the healthiest way to spend an evening?
qa.e: Outdoor play keeps the body active. Long screen time and late nights are not healthy.

qa.q: Which of these is an Indian outdoor game?
qa.e: Kho-kho is a running and chasing game played in teams.

qa.q: How does yoga help us?
qa.a: It makes the body flexible and calms the mind
qa.e: Yoga stretches the body and slow breathing helps the mind feel calm.

qa.q: Rohan plays for 40 minutes before school. How many more minutes of play does he need to make one hour?
qa.e: One hour is 60 minutes. 60 − 40 = 20 minutes more.

qa.q: Which of these is a feeling?
qa.e: Excited is a feeling. Table, mango and bicycle are things.

qa.q: Kunal feels very angry. What is a good thing to do?
qa.a: Take slow deep breaths and count to ten
qa.e: Deep breaths and counting help us calm down before we speak or act.

qa.q: Who is a trusted adult you can share worries with?
qa.e: Parents, grandparents and teachers know you and want to keep you safe.

qa.q: A new girl in class sits alone at lunch. What is the kind thing to do?
qa.a: Invite her to sit and eat with you
qa.e: Inviting her to join makes her feel welcome and happy.

qa.q: Someone in the bus touches you in a way that makes you feel unsafe. What should you do?
qa.a: Say 'No', move away and tell a trusted adult
qa.e: Your body belongs to you. Say no, get away and tell an adult you trust.

qa.q: Are feelings like sadness and fear normal?
qa.e: All people have all kinds of feelings. They are a normal part of life.

qa.q: Priya's friend is crying because she lost a race. What can Priya say?
qa.a: 'It's okay. You ran really well. Let's practise together.'
qa.e: Kind, encouraging words help a friend feel better.

qa.q: Why is it good to talk about our worries?
qa.a: It makes worries feel lighter and others can help
qa.e: Sharing a worry with someone you trust can make you feel better, and they may help solve it.

qa.q: What does a simple machine do?
qa.e: Simple machines help us lift, move or cut things with less effort.

qa.q: The fixed point on which a lever turns is called the…
qa.e: A lever turns on a point called the fulcrum, like the middle of a seesaw.

qa.q: Which simple machine is used to pull a bucket of water up from a well?
qa.e: The rope runs over a grooved wheel. Pulling down on the rope lifts the bucket up.

qa.q: A seesaw is an example of a…
qa.e: A seesaw is a long bar resting on a fulcrum in the middle. That makes it a lever.

qa.q: Which of these uses a wheel and axle?
qa.e: A bicycle's wheels turn on rods called axles.

qa.q: A pair of scissors is made of how many levers?
qa.e: Scissors have two blades, each a lever, joined at a pin which acts as the fulcrum.

qa.q: Why do we use a bottle opener instead of our fingers to open a bottle cap?
qa.e: A bottle opener is a lever. It gives a bigger push on the cap with less effort.

qa.q: When you pull the rope of a flagpole pulley downwards, the flag moves…
qa.e: A pulley changes the direction of the pull. Pulling down sends the flag up.

qa.q: What is another name for a ramp?
qa.e: A ramp is a sloping flat surface, also called an inclined plane.

qa.q: Which simple machine is a knife?
qa.e: A knife is thin and sharp at its edge. It is a wedge that pushes things apart as it cuts.

qa.q: Workers roll a heavy drum up a plank into a truck. Which simple machine is the plank?
qa.e: The sloping plank is an inclined plane. It makes moving the drum up easier.

qa.q: A jar lid turns round and round to close tightly. It works like a…
qa.e: The lid and the jar have grooves that wind around, like a screw.

qa.q: Why do hospitals have ramps?
qa.a: So wheelchairs and stretchers can move in easily
qa.e: Wheels can roll up a ramp but not up steps, so ramps help everyone enter.

qa.q: Which part of an axe makes it a wedge?
qa.e: A wedge is thick at one end and thin at the other. The sharp edge splits the wood.

qa.q: When we use a ramp instead of lifting a box straight up, what changes?
qa.a: We need less effort but move it a longer distance
qa.e: A ramp spreads the work over a longer path, so each push is easier.

qa.q: Which of these is an inclined plane?
qa.e: A slide is a smooth slope, which is an inclined plane.

qa.q: A push or a pull is called a…
qa.e: Any push or pull is a force.

qa.q: How does a swing move?
qa.e: A swing goes forward and back again and again. That is to and fro motion.

qa.q: Which of these is a pull?
qa.a: Opening a drawer by its handle
qa.e: To open a drawer, we pull it towards us.

qa.q: Rani presses a lump of clay with her thumb and it gets a dent. What did the force do?
qa.e: A push can change the shape of soft things like clay.

qa.q: Why are heavy boxes easier to move on a trolley with wheels?
qa.e: Wheels roll instead of rubbing along the floor, so less force is needed.

qa.q: The blades of a ceiling fan move…
qa.e: Fan blades turn in circles around the centre. That is round and round motion.

qa.q: A ball is rolled with the same push on two surfaces. On which will it go the farthest?
qa.e: Grass, sand and mud are rough and slow the ball down. A smooth floor slows it the least.

qa.q: A cricketer hits a ball and it changes direction. What made it change direction?
qa.e: The bat pushes the ball with a force, which changes its direction.

qa.q: What is a raw material?
qa.a: The basic thing from which a product is made
qa.e: A raw material is what we start with to make a product, like cotton for cloth.

qa.q: Glass is made mainly from…
qa.e: Sand is heated to a very high temperature in factories to make glass.

qa.q: Which raw material comes from an animal?
qa.e: Wool comes from the hair of sheep and some goats.

qa.q: Jaggery (gur) is made from the juice of…
qa.e: Sugarcane juice is boiled until it becomes thick, and then it sets as jaggery.

qa.q: Silk comes from…
qa.e: Silkworms spin cocoons of fine thread. The thread is taken off and woven into silk.

qa.q: Paper is made from the pulp of…
qa.e: Wood or bamboo is mashed into pulp, which is pressed and dried into paper.

qa.q: In 'cotton → shirt', which one is the product?
qa.e: The shirt is the new thing made from cotton, so the shirt is the product.

qa.q: Which of these comes from the earth?
qa.e: Clay is a kind of soil, so it comes from the earth.

qa.q: What is used to weave thread into cloth?
qa.e: A loom is a frame on which threads are woven together to make cloth.

qa.q: What is the hot oven in which pots are baked called?
qa.e: Potters bake their pots in a very hot oven called a kiln.

qa.q: Which step comes just after removing seeds from cotton?
qa.e: After the seeds are removed, the cotton is spun into thread. Then it is woven.

qa.q: What does a potter use to give clay a round shape?
qa.e: The potter's wheel spins round and round, so the potter's hands can shape the clay evenly.

qa.q: Why is wheat ground in a mill?
qa.e: Grinding turns hard wheat grains into soft flour, which can be made into dough.

qa.q: Mahatma Gandhi used a charkha. What does a charkha do?
qa.e: A charkha is a spinning wheel. It twists cotton fibres into thread.

qa.q: What would happen if a potter baked a pot before shaping it?
qa.a: The clay would become hard and could not be shaped
qa.e: Baking makes clay hard, so it must be shaped first. The order of steps matters.

qa.q: Which is the last step in making a roti?
qa.a: Cooking it on a hot tawa
qa.e: The rolled roti is cooked on a hot tawa at the very end.

qa.q: Madhubani painting comes from which state?
qa.e: Madhubani paintings, with bright colours and patterns, come from the Mithila region of Bihar.

qa.q: Channapatna in Karnataka is famous for…
qa.e: Channapatna makes colourful, smooth wooden toys.

qa.q: What is Bandhani?
qa.a: A tie-and-dye way of colouring cloth
qa.e: In Bandhani, small parts of cloth are tied tightly before dyeing, making dotted patterns.

qa.q: Kanchipuram in Tamil Nadu is famous for…
qa.e: Kanchipuram silk sarees are woven with rich colours and designs.

qa.q: How is a factory different from a cottage industry?
qa.a: A factory uses big machines to make many things quickly
qa.e: Cottage industries work by hand at home or in small workshops. Factories use machines.

qa.q: Warli paintings, made with simple circles, triangles and lines, come from…
qa.e: Warli art from Maharashtra uses simple shapes to show people, animals and daily life.

qa.q: Why is it good to buy handmade crafts?
qa.a: It helps artists earn and keeps old skills alive
qa.e: When people buy crafts, artists can earn a living and keep their skills going.

qa.q: Blue pottery is a famous craft of which city?
qa.e: Jaipur in Rajasthan is well known for its blue and white pottery.

qa.q: Which animal is called the ship of the desert?
qa.e: Camels can walk long distances on hot sand, carrying people and loads like a ship on the sea.

qa.q: What does a camel's hump store?
qa.e: The hump stores fat. The camel can use it for energy when food is scarce.

qa.q: The Thar Desert is mostly in which state?
qa.e: Most of the Thar Desert lies in western Rajasthan.

qa.q: Why do desert houses have thick mud walls and small windows?
qa.a: To keep the inside cool during hot days
qa.e: Thick walls and small windows stop the heat from coming in quickly.

qa.q: Why do the camel's wide, padded feet help in the desert?
qa.a: They do not sink in soft sand
qa.e: Wide feet spread the camel's weight, so it can walk on soft sand without sinking.

qa.q: How do people in the desert save water?
qa.a: They collect rainwater in tanks and step-wells
qa.e: Since rain is rare, people store every drop in tanks and step-wells.

qa.q: What is a bhunga?
qa.a: A round mud house in Kutch
qa.e: Bhungas are round houses with mud walls and cone-shaped roofs in Kutch, Gujarat.

qa.q: Why can desert nights be cold after a very hot day?
qa.a: The sand loses its heat quickly after sunset
qa.e: Sand heats up fast in the sun and cools down fast after sunset.

qa.q: Why do houses in snowy hills have sloping roofs?
qa.a: So that rain and snow slide off
qa.e: On a sloping roof, rain and snow slide down instead of piling up.

qa.q: What is terrace farming?
qa.a: Growing crops on step-like fields cut into hills
qa.e: In terrace farming, slopes are cut into flat steps so crops can grow.

qa.q: Which animal gives milk and wool and carries loads in the high Himalayas?
qa.e: Yaks have long thick hair and can live in very cold, high places.

qa.q: Apples grow well in which state?
qa.e: The cool hills of Himachal Pradesh are famous for apples.

qa.q: What kind of clothes do people in cold hills usually wear in winter?
qa.e: Woollen clothes keep the body warm in the cold.

qa.q: Darjeeling and the Nilgiris are famous for growing…
qa.e: Tea plants grow well on the cool, rainy slopes of these hills.

qa.q: As you go higher up a mountain, the air usually becomes…
qa.e: High places are cooler. That is why mountain tops can have snow.

qa.q: Hill houses are often built with…
qa.e: Wood and stone are found nearby in the hills and make strong houses.

qa.q: What is the coast?
qa.e: The coast is the strip of land that meets the sea.

qa.q: Which state makes the most salt in India?
qa.e: Gujarat, with its long coast and hot sun, makes most of India's salt.

qa.q: What is the main job of many people living by the sea?
qa.e: The sea is full of fish, so fishing is a main job on the coast.

qa.q: Which tree grows in large numbers along the coasts of Kerala and Goa?
qa.e: Coconut trees grow well in warm, wet coastal places.

qa.q: The weather on the coast is often warm and humid. What does humid mean?
qa.a: The air has a lot of moisture
qa.e: Humid air has a lot of water vapour in it, so it feels damp and sticky.

qa.q: How is salt made from sea water?
qa.a: The sun dries up the water and salt is left behind
qa.e: In salt pans, the sun dries the water away, leaving salt crystals.

qa.q: Houseboats on calm backwaters are a famous sight in which state?
qa.e: Kerala's backwaters are famous for their houseboats.

qa.q: Why do many coastal houses in Kerala have sloping roofs?
qa.a: So that heavy rain water flows off quickly
qa.e: Kerala gets heavy monsoon rain, so sloping roofs let the water run off.

qa.q: What does 'adapt' mean?
qa.a: To change our ways to suit the place
qa.e: Adapting means changing houses, clothes, food or body features to suit the surroundings.

qa.q: Why are some houses in flood-prone parts of Assam built on stilts?
qa.a: So that flood water flows under the house
qa.e: The stilts keep the house above the water during floods.

qa.q: How do a camel's long eyelashes help it?
qa.a: They keep sand out of its eyes
qa.e: In sandy winds, long eyelashes protect the camel's eyes.

qa.q: Ladakh is called a cold desert because…
qa.a: it is very cold and gets very little rain
qa.e: A desert is a place with very little rain. Ladakh is dry and also very cold.

qa.q: Which animal of Ladakh gives very soft, warm pashmina wool?
qa.e: Pashmina goats grow soft, warm wool to survive the cold winters of Ladakh.

qa.q: What is climate?
qa.a: The usual weather of a place over many years
qa.e: Weather changes daily, but climate is the usual pattern of a place over many years.

qa.q: Which of these would suit a person living in a hot, dry place?
qa.e: Loose cotton clothes let air flow and keep the body cool in the heat.

qa.q: How does a yak's thick, long hair help it?
qa.a: It keeps the yak warm in the cold mountains
qa.e: Thick hair traps warmth, so the yak can live in freezing high places.

qa.q: What is the sun?
qa.e: The sun is a star, a huge ball of hot, glowing gas.

qa.q: Why does the moon shine?
qa.a: Sunlight falls on it and bounces back
qa.e: The moon has no light of its own. It reflects the light of the sun.

qa.q: Why does the sun look small in the sky?
qa.a: Because it is very far away
qa.e: The sun is far bigger than the Earth. It only looks small because it is so far away.

qa.q: The Pole Star helps travellers find which direction?
qa.e: The Pole Star (Dhruv Tara) stays above the North, so it shows the North direction.

qa.q: How many bright stars make the Saptarishi pattern?
qa.e: 'Sapta' means seven. The Saptarishi is a pattern of seven bright stars.

qa.q: On which date in 2023 did India's Chandrayaan-3 land on the moon?
qa.e: Chandrayaan-3's lander Vikram landed near the moon's south pole on 23 August 2023. India celebrates this day as National Space Day.

qa.q: Why must we never look straight at the sun?
qa.a: It can badly hurt our eyes
qa.e: The sun's light is so strong that it can damage our eyes, even with sunglasses.

qa.q: What goes around the Earth?
qa.e: The moon goes around the Earth. The Earth goes around the sun.

qa.q: What causes day and night?
qa.e: As the Earth spins, each place turns towards the sun (day) and then away from it (night).

qa.q: About how many hours does the Earth take to spin around once?
qa.e: One full spin of the Earth takes about 24 hours, which is one day and one night.

qa.q: About how many days does the Earth take to go once around the sun?
qa.e: The Earth takes about 365 days to go around the sun. That is one year.

qa.q: What is the shape of the Earth?
qa.e: The Earth is round like a ball. That is why only half of it gets sunlight at a time.

qa.q: In which direction does the sun seem to rise?
qa.e: The Earth spins from west to east, so the sun seems to come up in the east.

qa.q: If it is daytime in India, what is it on the side of the Earth facing away from the sun?
qa.e: The side facing away from the sun gets no sunlight, so it has night.

qa.q: A torch is shone on a spinning ball in a dark room. What does the torch stand for?
qa.e: The torch gives light like the sun, and the ball is like the Earth.

qa.q: How many hours are there in 3 full days?
qa.e: Each day has 24 hours. 24 × 3 = 72 hours.

qa.q: What are the phases of the moon?
qa.a: The different shapes of the moon we see during a month
qa.e: Phases are the changing shapes of the moon's lit part that we see from the Earth.

qa.q: On which night can we NOT see the moon?
qa.e: On the new moon night, the lit side of the moon faces away from the Earth.

qa.q: About how many days pass from one full moon to the next?
qa.e: The moon takes about 29 and a half days to go through all its phases.

qa.q: Does the moon really change its shape?
qa.a: No, we only see different amounts of its lit part
qa.e: The moon is always round. Its lit part faces us by different amounts.

qa.q: Diwali is celebrated on a new moon night. What will the sky look like on Diwali night?
qa.e: On a new moon night, the moon is not seen. The lamps make Diwali night bright!

qa.q: Which shape comes after the new moon as the moon starts to grow?
qa.e: After the new moon, a thin curved crescent appears first, then it grows.

qa.q: Why is half of the moon always lit?
qa.a: The sun always shines on the half facing it
qa.e: Like the Earth, the moon has a sunny side. The half facing the sun is always lit.

qa.q: A full moon is seen on day 0. On about which day will the next full moon come?
qa.e: The full cycle takes about 29 and a half days, so the next full moon comes on day 29 or 30.
